text: The Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology Self-Report (IDS-SR) is a widely used self-report instrument that aligns with DSM criteria. It is designed for screening and assessing depression severity [ 19 , 20 ]. The scale includes 30 items and yields a total score from 0 to 84. A cutoff score of ≥ 18 on the IDS-SR indicates clinically relevant depressive symptoms [ 20 ]. The IDS-SR assesses not only typical depressive and anxiety symptoms but also atypical manifestations. Its factor structure includes three dimensions: “mood/cognition”, “anxiety/somatic”, and “sleep” [ 20 , 21 ]. Each dimension can function as a separate subscale to assess the severity of specific symptom clusters. This multidimensional structure distinguishes the IDS-SR from other tools, such as the Centre for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), GDS, and HRSD. Previous studies have shown that the IDS-SR has good reliability and validity in both clinical and community samples. It has also been validated for use in older adults [ 20 , 22 ].
